title: Facet load share at L3-L4, L4-L5 - Ivicsics M, Bishop N, Puschel K, Morlock M, Huber G 2014 (J Biomech 47:1712) (secondary, Ghezelbash 2020 review)
condition: intact disc, capsular ligaments intact (resection study)

quantity.name: facet load share
quantity.definition: percentage of applied axial compression carried by both facet joints, median (min/max); level printed as 'L3-L5 & L4-L5' in the review

source.authors: Ghezelbash F, Schmidt H, Shirazi-Adl A, El-Rich M
source.sample: not stated in review (see primary: Ivicsics M, Bishop N, Puschel K, Morlock M, Huber G 2014 (J Biomech 47:1712)); human cadaveric lumbar specimens of Ivicsics M, Bishop N, Puschel K, Morlock M, Huber G 2014 (J Biomech 47:1712), as compiled in Ghezelbash et al. 2020 Table 2

protocol.summary: 700 N compression with 5 deg imposed extension or flexion; % of compression carried by both facets (not force in N).
how_to_simulate: Apply 700 N axial compression with 5 deg extension or 5 deg flexion
Compute the sum of both facet contact forces as % of the applied compression
protocol.notes: Secondary data compiled in a review (the user's own review). Sample size, specimen age, rate and cycles are not given in the review; use the primary paper for these. Primary source: Ivicsics M, Bishop N, Puschel K, Morlock M, Huber G 2014 (J Biomech 47:1712).

extraction.from: Table 2 (summary of in vitro facet force measurements)
extraction.check_notes: Re-read against the rendered Table 2 image (page 5, 200 dpi): every value, +/-, min/max, units and level labels match the pdftotext output.

pass_rule.rule: |model-mean| <= 1 SD (mean+/-SD) or min <= model <= max (ranges); widen for facet-force method bias (Wilson 2006)

shared_sample_with: ivicsics2014: primary (fe_facet tests from Ivicsics2014.pdf, other fork)
